name: Thinking Out Loud: Do Reasoning Models Know When They're Right?
authors: Qingcheng Zeng, Weihao Xuan (co-first), Leyang Cui, Rob Voigt; lead affiliation Northwestern University (with University of Tokyo / RIKEN AIP, Westlake University, UC Davis)
venue: EMNLP 2025 (Main), Proceedings of the 2025 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing, pp. 1394-1407 (arXiv:2504.06564, submitted Apr 2025)
reflection_type: calibration/probing — analysis of verbalized confidence (verbalized uncertainty) as a lens onto the self-reflective behavior of large reasoning models; it is an empirical analysis paper, not a self-correction method. It also tests a self-reflection prompting strategy (two-round dialogue eliciting an answer then a confidence self-assessment) as one of three prompting conditions.
feedback_source: self-generated (models verbalize their own confidence / 'I don't know' decisions); calibration is then scored against ground-truth correctness as an evaluation oracle (the model receives no feedback signal — this is measurement, not training).
iteration_structure: single-shot (the analysis itself is one-pass evaluation per prompt). One of the three prompting strategies (self-reflection / SR) uses a two-round dialogue: round one elicits the answer, round two elicits a confidence self-evaluation.
reflection_object: reasoning chain and output content — the study reflects on the model's verbalized confidence about its own answer and on the long chain-of-thought reasoning trace (analyzing how chain length relates to confidence, accuracy, and calibration). No artifact (prompt, skill, weights) is modified by the paper itself; it analyzes models produced by SFT-distillation and RL.
requires_training: none (the paper performs no training; it analyzes off-the-shelf models). The analysis contrasts three training pipelines of the studied models: instruct models (SFT + general/alignment RL), SFT reasoning models (distillation on long CoT traces), and RL reasoning models (reasoning RL on top of the distilled models).
reward_or_critic_model: self-as-judge (models verbalize their own confidence); ground-truth correctness is used only to score calibration, not as a reward. No trained reward or critic model is introduced.
distillation_target: none — the paper does not distill reflection into a reusable artifact. It studies models whose reasoning was created via distillation (R1-Distill-Qwen on 800k traces) and reasoning RL, but produces no new artifact itself.
emergent_vs_engineered: Analyzes RL-emergent self-reflective behavior in large reasoning models (o1/R1-style 'Wait, but...' introspection) rather than prompt/scaffold-engineered reflection like Reflexion; the finding is that distillation + RL progressively shape (and in factuality settings erode) calibration. The self-reflection prompting strategy it also tests is prompt-engineered, but the paper's central object is the emergent reflective behavior.
memory_type: none (no memory mechanism; single-pass evaluation study)
error_localization_granularity: holistic/outcome-level — calibration (ECE/ACE) and failure prediction (AUROC, AUPRC) are computed at the whole-response/answer level; confidence is verbalized for the final answer, not per reasoning step. The chain-length analysis associates accuracy/confidence with overall trace length (response-level), not token-level attribution.
intra_task_vs_inter_task: n/a (analysis paper, not a learning method); the closest framing is cross-domain generalization — RL-trained calibration gains transfer across domains (e.g., math-RL improving science-reasoning calibration).
failure_recovery_vs_avoidance: n/a — the paper studies whether models recognize their knowledge boundaries and abstain ('I don't know' / 'not attempted'); it finds LRMs abstain less (avoidance failure), but it is an analysis, not a recovery/avoidance method.
task_domains: QA/reasoning (math, scientific reasoning, general logical reasoning) and factuality QA. Code reasoning was excluded because most models could not emit code and a confidence score simultaneously.
benchmarks: AIME 2024 & AIME 2025 (math, 30 questions each, 5 runs); GPQA-Diamond (198 graduate-level science MCQs) and SuperGPQA (1500 sampled questions); LiveBench-Reasoning (150 reasoning problems); SimpleQA and FreshQA (FreshQA-2025-04-28) for factuality.
headline_result: Reasoning-oriented training laddered up calibration on reasoning-heavy tasks but eroded knowledge-boundary awareness on factuality. Example: R1-Distill-Qwen-32B vs Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct on AIME — accuracy 9.67% -> 65.7%, ECE 0.752 -> 0.240, AUROC 0.695 -> 0.813 (vanilla CoT). On factuality, LRMs gave far fewer 'not attempted'/'I don't know' answers (32B: instruct 2492 vs SFT-reasoning 76 vs RL-reasoning 63 over SimpleQA+FreshQA) without commensurate accuracy gains except DeepSeek-R1 — a 'reasoning tax.'
baselines: Within-architecture comparison across three model types: instruct models (Qwen2.5-14B/32B-Instruct, DeepSeek-V3) vs SFT reasoning models (DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-14B/32B) vs RL reasoning models (DeepCoder-14B-Preview, Skywork-OR1-32B-Preview, DeepSeek-R1). Three prompting strategies compared: vanilla CoT, vanilla CoT with probability mass, and self-reflection.
gains_vs_baseline: On reasoning benchmarks, RL reasoning models beat SFT-only counterparts: e.g., Skywork-32B vs R1-Distill-Qwen-32B on AIME ECE 0.183 vs 0.240, AUROC 0.928 vs 0.813; on LiveBench-Reasoning Skywork ECE 0.074 vs 0.152. SFT over instruct gave the largest jump (32B AIME ECE 0.752->0.240). On factuality the pattern reverses for small models — a U-shaped calibration trajectory (instruct -> SFT-reasoning worsens -> RL-reasoning partially recovers): e.g., 32B SimpleQA+FreshQA shared-question ECE 0.591 (instruct) -> 0.640 (SFT) -> 0.600 (RL); DeepSeek-R1 shared ECE 0.496 -> 0.317 vs DeepSeek-V3.
compute_cost_profile: Inference allows up to 32,000 new tokens per generation at temperature 0.6; reasoning models emit long CoT chains so token cost is much higher than single-pass instruct answers. The self-reflection prompting strategy doubles the dialogue (two rounds). No training conducted by the authors. Chain-length analysis: longer chains (>10,000 tokens) correlate with lower accuracy and increased ECE for small-scale models.
known_limitations: Code reasoning excluded (most models could not output a code snippet plus a confidence score together). Factuality outputs were auto-graded following Wei et al. (SimpleQA protocol) without human verification. Findings about reduced knowledge-boundary awareness ('reasoning tax') are strongest for small-scale (14B/32B) open-source LRMs; large-scale DeepSeek-R1 mostly avoids the degradation. Studies open-source LRMs only on the reasoning RL side; calibration is sensitive to prompt design.
oracle_or_external_feedback_dependency: intrinsic-only for the model behavior studied (verbalized confidence is fully self-generated); ground-truth labels are used only as an evaluation oracle to compute calibration/failure-prediction metrics, not as feedback to the model.
self_correction_efficacy: task-dependent — reasoning-oriented training improves calibration (self-assessment) on reasoning-heavy tasks but degrades knowledge-boundary recognition on factuality for small-scale models (the 'reasoning tax'); large-scale RL models (DeepSeek-R1) recover. Not a self-correction method per se, so framed as a calibration/awareness effect.
calibration_effect: mixed — improves on reasoning-heavy benchmarks (math/science/general reasoning), in a progressive laddered fashion instruct < SFT-reasoning < RL-reasoning; degrades/overconfident on factuality for small-scale models ('reasoning tax', far fewer 'I don't know' responses), with partial U-shaped recovery under RL and full recovery at large scale (DeepSeek-R1).
failure_attribution_capability: n/a (not a failure-attribution study; it diagnoses a calibration/knowledge-boundary failure mode rather than attributing responsibility to agents or steps)
failure_mode_addressed: Diminished awareness of knowledge boundaries / over-attempting (very low 'I don't know'/'not attempted' rates) leading to confident hallucination on factuality tasks — a 'reasoning tax' (related to the 'hallucination tax' discussed in Song et al. and Kirichenko et al. AbstentionBench). Also documents overconfidence with shorter/less-elaborate reasoning, and a length-vs-accuracy degradation (overthinking) where longer chains correlate with lower accuracy.
builds_on: DeepSeek-R1 (DeepSeek-AI 2025) and o1 (OpenAI 2024) reasoning-model paradigm; R1-Distill-Qwen, DeepCoder-14B, Skywork-OR1 as evaluated models; verbalized confidence / calibration literature (Tian et al. 2023; Xiong et al. 2024; Yang et al. 2024); SimpleQA (Wei et al. 2024) and FreshQA (Vu et al. 2023) factuality protocols; ECE (Guo et al. 2017) and ACE (Nixon et al. 2019); DeepSeek-R1 Thoughtology (Marjanović et al. 2025) for the chain-length analysis; Chu et al. 2025 ('SFT memorizes, RL generalizes').
extended_by_or_inspired: Connects to concurrent and follow-on work on the 'hallucination tax' / abstention failures of RL reasoning models: Song et al. (2025), Kirichenko et al. (2025, AbstentionBench), Kalai et al. (2025, 'Why Language Models Hallucinate'), Mei et al. (2025), Yoon et al. (2025), and Tu et al. (2025) on reward design for uncertainty. (Specific named successors citing this paper not individually confirmed; cited 12 times per Semantic Scholar.)
reasoning_model_native: true — the paper specifically targets large reasoning models (o1/R1-era) with built-in long-CoT self-reflective behavior, contrasting them against instruct models to isolate the effect of reasoning-oriented distillation and RL on verbalized calibration.
on_policy_distillation_link: Indirectly relevant: the SFT reasoning models studied (R1-Distill-Qwen-14B/32B) are off-policy distillation on 800k R1-generated traces (600k long reasoning chains + 200k non-reasoning), and the RL reasoning models add reasoning RL on top. The paper frames distillation as 'memorize' (in-domain calibration gains, factuality calibration loss) vs RL as 'generalize' (domain-agnostic calibration recovery), echoing Chu et al. (2025). No explicit on-policy-distillation method is used.
sample_efficiency: n/a (analysis paper, no learning trials). Evaluation protocol: AIME and LiveBench-Reasoning run 5 times and aggregated; GPQA-Diamond 198 items, SuperGPQA 1500 sampled items, M=10 calibration bins.
